critical.issue: With the RESTORED default config (gemini-3-flash-preview + max_tokens=1400) the analyze prompt consistently truncates the model output before the closing JSON brace, causing '_run_llm → No JSON in AI response' and a 424 back to the client on every real (non-quota-exhausted) call. Verified: 3 consecutive analyze calls all failed with `AI error (gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview): No JSON in AI response`; raising max_tokens to 8000 (temporarily via PUT /admin/ai/config) makes analyze succeed with valid JSON. gemini-3-flash-preview is a reasoning model — 1400 tokens is not enough headroom for the analyze system prompt + strict-JSON output. This is a user-visible production defect: any end user in demo mode (and likely in live mode too) will see a 424 with the fallback friendly message 'AI error (gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview): No JSON in AI response' on Analyze. Recommend raising default max_tokens to >= 4000 for reasoning-capable models OR adding a retry-with-larger-max_tokens fallback OR asking the model for JSON via structured output.

minor.issue: The owner's Gemini API key hit a real 429 quota after ~10 test calls in ~5 minutes (message: 'gemini rate limit / quota exceeded for model gemini-3-flash-preview'). This is upstream Google quota, but the app has no client-side back-off / caching for the /admin/ai/test PONG probe — every click of Test Connection burns a quota unit. Consider caching the last test result for N seconds.

DEPRECATED_MODELS dict is defined AFTER put_ai_config uses it (line 543 refs a name defined at line 551). It works only because put_ai_config is imported/called at request-time (Python resolves globals lazily), but the ordering is fragile — move DEPRECATED_MODELS above the route.

TestServiceNowConfig.test_get_default_config, test_put_preserves_config, TestAIConfig.test_get_ai_config assert default OpenAI provider — env is intentionally gemini per task requirements. Update those assertions or mark xfail.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py still 1210 lines — split into routers (>700-line guideline).
DEPRECATED_MODELS defined after its first use inside put_ai_config — works only due to lazy global resolution; readability & static-analysis smell.

_friendly_ai_error uses substring matching on str(e) — fragile if litellm changes wording (e.g. 'NotFoundError' vs 'Not found'). Prefer inspecting exception class / status_code fields exposed by emergentintegrations.

AIConfig.jsx: `if (cfg.model && !models.includes(cfg.model)) models.push(cfg.model);` mutates the shared MODELS[provider] array via reference — repeated renders/provider switches can leak values into MODELS. Copy first: `const models = [...(MODELS[cfg.provider]||[])];`.

analyze() persists the fallback stub analysis (status='error') with the friendly detail text embedded in the JSON before raising 424 — the record ends up on /admin/analyses & /my-analysis with a fake-looking body ('AI analysis unavailable: …'). Consider omitting or clearly flagging 'error' records in the UI.

rca_of_the_issue: gemini-3-flash-preview is a reasoning model whose completion budget (max_tokens) covers hidden reasoning tokens too. The analyze system prompt (STRICT JSON with 6 keys + evidence context) needs ~2-3k output tokens; 1400 leaves the JSON truncated before its closing brace, so `re.search(r'\{[\s\S]*\}', raw)` fails and _run_llm raises 'No JSON in AI response' → 424. Reproduction: PUT ai config with max_tokens=1400 (restored default), demo mode (instance_url=''), POST /api/incidents/sn_inc_0001/analyze as any end user → 424 every time. Mitigation options: (a) bump default max_tokens to 4000-8000 for gemini-3-flash-preview / any *-preview reasoning model; (b) call the model with structured-output JSON schema so partial responses still parse; (c) retry once with a larger cap when the extractor fails.
